neighbours.label: the words ' hung' (hung over, hung on a wall, hung up on) and ' hit' in the passive sense of being struck by misfortune ('were hit hardest'), as against an active physical hit or 'hungry'
fire: Coastal villages were hit hardest when the river burst its banks in March.
She stayed in bed until noon, badly hung over from the wedding.
A faded portrait of his grandfather hung above the kitchen door.
Small bakeries have been hit hard by the rising price of flour.
Two lanterns hung from the branches of the old oak tree.
He felt hung over and slow all through the Monday meeting.
Farmers in the south were hit by a second year of drought.
Heavy curtains hung across the windows to keep out the cold.
quiet: Coastal villages held a festival when the river was cleaned in March.
She stayed in bed until noon, tired out from the wedding.
A faded portrait of his grandfather leans against the kitchen door.
Small bakeries have been selling more bread since the price of flour fell.
Two lanterns are hanging from the branches of the old oak tree.
He felt hungry and slow all through the Monday meeting.
The striker hit the crossbar twice in the second half.
Heavy curtains were drawn across the windows to keep out the cold.
